title: Enjoying Discipling My Wife
author: Justin Myko Agpangan
summary: Writing just over a month into his marriage, Justin Myko Agpangan reflects on the joy of leading his wife in daily Bible study and prayer. He describes their progress through 1 Corinthians, his practice of explaining and applying each passage, and the way his wife's own insights edify him in turn, presenting the practice as mutual rather than one-directional. His argument is that while spouses should each study Scripture individually, married couples should also carve out intentional shared time in the Word as a special means of grace. Agpangan repeats his framing of husbands as God's spokesmen or prophets in the home, bound to the completed canon rather than new revelation, and stresses there is no one-size-fits-all formula: even ten minutes at meals, done daily, has a cumulative effect. The piece closes on spiritual intimacy as a deeper intimacy cultivated through family worship, which he says both deepens the couple's roots in God and increases their enjoyment of each other.
points: Agpangan presents discipling one's wife as mutually edifying: he explains and applies the text, asks her thoughts, and is instructed by her insights.
He distinguishes individual Bible study from shared study, arguing married couples need intentional time in Scripture together.
Husbands are framed as prophets in the home only as spokesmen for completed Scripture, not recipients of new revelation.
Consistency matters more than length; short daily sessions produce a cumulative spiritual effect.
He argues spiritual intimacy cultivated through shared worship is a deeper intimacy that also increases a couple's enjoyment of one another.
quotes: I heartily enjoy the time that I have spent discipling my wife. We are now in 1 Corinthians 14. We just finished verse 25 of the said chapter yesterday.

She listens as I explain and apply the passage. And then from time to time, I try to ask her thoughts about the passage that we are studying. She also gladly shares her thoughts of the passage to me. I am also edified by my wife's insights.
In marriage, there's a time when each spouse study the Bible separately. However, there's also a time when both spouses should carve out intentional time to study God's Word together.

We need the sufficient revelation in the Bible and use it to speak to our wives and children (for others; please also pray with us with regards to this). We have a prophetic role in a sense that we are God's spokesmen in our home.

There is no one-size fits all formula. The important thing is that we are doing our best to do this daily even for a short time. The cumulative effect of doing this in our souls is incalculable but very profitable.

Spiritual intimacy is worth having. This is a deeper kind of intimacy; an intimacy that cuts deeper in our souls. And we cultivate this through daily family worship, communing with God together in His Word and prayer.
